description: ⚑ TWO LIMBS, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS DESIRED BEHAVIOUR. (1) COUNTER-GATE, correct: a line of prose spelling `keyword (…)` followed on the NEXT line by a DECLARATION must NOT fire E-CONTROL-FLOW-IN-MARKUP — an unbounded recognizer head joined the prose's `)` to the declaration's `{` and the recovery then DELETED the declaration. (2) ⚑ OPEN DEFECT, pinned as CURRENT behaviour and NOT endorsed: `function greet()` is NOT compiled here. The preceding prose line silently disables the §40.8 auto-lift for the rest of the run, so what appears in the emitted page is the declaration's SOURCE TEXT as inert prose — `greet` is absent from the client JS entirely, and the file emits ZERO diagnostics.
rationale: ⚑ READ LIMB 2 BEFORE READING THIS CASE AS A SUCCESS. An earlier revision of this rationale said the declaration 'must survive into the emitted page', and that wording was FALSE IN THE WAY THAT MATTERS: what survives is inert page text, not a working declaration. Under §62.2 the corpus is the versioned contract, so leaving it stated that way froze a defect in as correct behaviour and would have blocked a fix with a green gate. MEASURED BY EXECUTION at S383, three compiles: (a) `<program>` + `function greet() { return 1 }` ALONE — greet IS lifted, appears in `case.client.js`, is ABSENT from `<body>`, and draws W-DEAD-FUNCTION + I-FN-PROMOTABLE; (b) the SAME declaration with ONE prose line above it — greet is absent from the client JS ENTIRELY, ships into `<body>` as literal page text, ZERO diagnostics; (c) prose + `<x> = 0` + a `${@x}` read — the structural state decl ships as page text and the READ fails E-STATE-UNDECLARED, so the compiler blames a correct line about a declaration that IS present in the source. Control: delete the prose line from (c) and it compiles clean. ⚑ THIS CONTRADICTS THE SPEC ON ITS OWN TERMS: §40.8's S123 amendment names `function name() { … }` / `fn name(…)` AND the structural state-decl form `<name> = expr` as members of the auto-lift set, with no positional qualifier. The mechanism is the same one that produces every other defect at this locus — `BARE_DECL_RE` is `^`-anchored against `block.raw`, and at a default-logic body-top a block-splitter text run is EVERY contiguous non-markup line, so ONE leading prose line takes the run-leading position and nothing below it is examined by any lift gate. ⚑ IF THAT DEFECT IS FIXED, THIS CASE IS ONE OF THE ONES TO FLIP, and flipping it needs a deliberate ruling rather than a silent green-to-green edit: limb 1 must stay green, and limb 2's `dom` body text must change to no longer contain the declaration source. Sibling pin for the statement variant of the same class: `ctrl-012-default-logic-non-leading-residual-neg`. ⚑ LIMB 1, WHY IT NEEDS ITS OWN CASE AND ITS OWN AXIS. `BARE_CONTROL_FLOW_IN_MARKUP_RE` was written for the S203 MARKUP locus, where a text run is element-delimited, so an unbounded lazy head (`\([^]*?\)`) was harmless there for years; reusing it at this locus, where a run spans lines, is what let the head cross a newline. The recognizer did not become wrong — its DOMAIN changed under it and nobody re-derived it. The 'ZERO corpus instances' figure that underwrote the landing was measured against a SINGLE-LINE shape and was therefore blind to this one: corpus-zero was never safety here. Re-measured over a purpose-built 78-fixture multi-line-prose corpus (8 prose openers × 9 followers plus residual and control shapes), the pre-fix build fired 13 times and DELETED a declaration in 8 fixtures the prior compiler kept. That is why limb 1 is pinned by an OUTPUT assertion and not only by a code count: a successor that applies the S203 reject-and-recover TEXT-DROP while emitting no diagnostic would delete the declaration and a codes-only case would stay green. ⚑ AND LIMB 1 HAS A TWIN AT THE OTHER LOCUS THAT THIS CASE DOES NOT GOVERN: a markup text run is element-delimited, so multi-line control flow THERE is real code that S203 has refused since S203. Applying this locus's single-line bound to the markup recognizer was MEASURED to re-open that gate, compiling multi-line and Allman shapes clean and shipping `if (` and an inner `${…}` into the page; pinned in `compiler/tests/unit/control-flow-in-markup-reject.test.js`. The two run-shapes need two rules; this case governs only the body-top one. The arm ruling 3 directed at this locus is HELD — see `docs/changes/ruling3-grammar-derived/PROBLEM-STATEMENT.md` for the full problem statement and the cross-axis matrix a successor owes. ⛑ THE `dom` ASSERTION IS WHAT MAKES BOTH LIMBS ENFORCED RATHER THAN NARRATED, and it is deliberately a WHOLE-TREE compare rather than `domAnchored`: the leaked declaration is a BARE TEXT NODE directly under `<body>` with no wrapping element, so no selector can address it — measured, `domAnchored` with `selector: "body"` reports 'no match' because the anchored root IS the body. The pinned value contains the declaration's SOURCE TEXT, which is itself the evidence for limb 2: a COMPILED function would not appear in `<body>` at all (measured in compile (a), where it does not). So the single assertion fails in BOTH directions that matter — a successor that text-drops the run deletes it, and a successor that correctly lifts it removes it from the body. The second is the intended FLIP. ⛑ S383 (R3) — `notCodePrefixes` MAKES THE SILENCE CLAIM ENFORCED RATHER THAN NARRATED. `codes: []` asserts NOTHING: `run.ts:441` computes `missing` by filtering the LISTED codes, so an empty list can never be violated, and `notCodes` constrains exactly one code. This case says the compiler is silent here, so it now forbids the whole `E-` and `W-` families (`run.ts:446-450`). MEASURED before pinning, through the runner rather than by hand: with `E-`, `W-` AND `I-` all forbidden, this case reports ZERO prefix violations. `I-` is deliberately left unpinned — the advisory/lint stream is a separate partition (S92/S93) and may legitimately gain hints at this locus without that being a regression here.
